SCHEMA 2 (MES-81 round 4, PM correction contract 26058-26060) changes three things from schema 1: (i) every boundary whose lib/ module produces the asserted artefact in BOTH directions is SPLIT into `(encode)` and `(decode)`; (ii) L2 runs at a MECHANICAL trigger — every boundary-direction whose live count is zero, never on a selection — and its result is recorded on every one, DEAD included; (iii) the round-2 dead boundaries are recorded here rather than in a prose side-note, so guard 20 reaches them. SCHEMA 3 (MES-88) changes two things from schema 2 and NOTHING else: (i) every boundary-direction gains `mutation_spec`, an APPLICABLE form of its `mutation` prose — a list of {file, from, to, occurrences, replace} applied by literal byte replacement — so the sweep can be RE-RUN from the repository rather than only read; (ii) `live_units` is COMPLETE on every row, closing the six-row sample described below. The `mutation` prose is UNCHANGED, byte for byte: `mutation_spec` is an addition, not a replacement, so the byte-comparison an AC1 re-run performs is about the bytes MES-81 actually committed and not about a re-serialisation. The two cannot drift because guard 27 requires every spec entry to render back to its prose line byte-for-byte, in order and in count.

procedure.L1: Mutate the boundary-direction, re-run THE WHOLE SUITE at seed 0, count what reddens OUTSIDE its own tests and outside the units of boundary-directions this table records dead. >=1 such unit => LIVE. L1 is a PROXY and its SILENCE IS AMBIGUOUS: it means either 'nothing routes this to a transport' or 'something does and no test asserts it'. THE POPULATION IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT: MES-81 measured over 979 units, MES-88 re-measured over 1021, and the difference is the suite growing, not lib/ moving. Schema 2 wrote '979' into this sentence, which read as a constant of the procedure rather than a fact about one run.
procedure.L2: Two conjuncts, and DEAD needs both. (a) BYTE PROBE — `mix run conformance/etcc_l2_probe.exs` drives 15 real lib/ entry points and prints the bytes they produce; the boundary's mutation is applied and the output diffed against the unmutated baseline. A scenario that MOVES is a lib/ call site routing the boundary to a transport, so the antecedent is FALSE and the verdict is LIVE. (b) CALL-SITE ENUMERATION — every lib/ reference to the boundary is listed (calls, `&Mod.fun/1` captures and dynamic dispatch included, and alias-aware per S7-16) and each caller followed to a live entry point or to a module lib/ never uses. (a) ALONE CANNOT ESTABLISH DEAD: the probe is server-side and its silence is another proxy. That is why every DEAD verdict below carries (b).
procedure.L2_trigger: MECHANICAL: L2 runs on EVERY boundary-direction whose live count is zero. Never on a selection. This is F6 (CODE_REVIEWER 26055, PM 26058): at round 3 the trigger was stated as 'where L1 is silent', L1 was silent twelve times and L2 was run on the three the sweeper suspected — S7-17 clause (ii) landing on the limb added to fix S7-17 clause (ii). Guard 20 makes it checkable: no boundary may be recorded DEAD without an L2 record.
procedure.counting: reddened_total counts failures the run reported WITH a file:line, which is how a failure is attributed. unlocated_failures is the remainder of the suite summary's own count — failures reported without a unit location. It never adds to the live count, so it can only make a LIVE verdict look weaker than it is, never make a DEAD one look stronger.
procedure.dead: potent AND L1 == 0 AND L2 negative on BOTH conjuncts.
procedure.expiry: docs/conformance/etcc-membership.md §2.3(e) as EXTENDED on MES-88 ([authored 26988 | ratified 26995]): a verdict expires when lib/ moves, AND ITS L1 MEASUREMENTS ADDITIONALLY EXPIRE WHEN THE UNIT POPULATION MOVES. So `verdict`, `established_by`, `direction` and the two l2 verdict fields are claims about lib/ and are what `mix conformance.sweep --check` compares; `suite_summary`, `reddened_total`, `reddened_by_module`, `reddened_outside_own`, `reddened_outside_own_and_dead` and `live_units` are functions of lib/ AND of the suite, and are reported as a stated delta. A test-only change can move a VERDICT in either direction, which is why the end-of-sprint cadence rule in CLAUDE.md tests the unit population as well as lib/.
procedure.live_units: COMPLETE on every row from MES-88 onward, and the completion is a disclosed byte change to six rows. Schema 2 capped it at 8 on the six single-direction boundaries the round-4 direction split did not re-measure — Meta 98/8, Dispatch 86/8, decode_message/1 64/8, Request 34/8, Notification 14/8, Client 12/8 — while every other row listed all of them. That was a round-3 residue, not a design choice, and under epic ruling 4 a field that reads as an enumeration and is a sample is the wrong shape. No verdict turned on it.
procedure.mutation_spec: SCHEMA 3. Each `mutation` prose line is `FILE: FROM  ->  TO` (the separator is exactly two spaces, an arrow, two spaces), and `mutation_spec` is its applicable reading: {file, from, to, occurrences, replace}. `occurrences` is how many times FROM occurs in FILE and is ASSERTED before anything is written (guard 26) — a different count means lib/ moved under the spec, and the sweep must fail LOUD rather than mutate something else. `replace` is "all" everywhere, and that is a MEASURED answer rather than a reading of the record: 16 of the 194 lines have a FROM occurring 2-6 times and nothing in the record said whether the sweeper replaced one or all. MES-88 ran BOTH readings on all 11 affected directions (`mix conformance.sweep --disambiguate`) and compared each against the committed `reddened_by_module`. "all" reproduced on 11 of 11; "first" reproduced on 6 and DIFFERED on 5 — Extensions 4 failures -> 0, Meta 135 -> 0, decode_message/1 69 -> 0, Types.Content (decode) 13 -> 9. That is S7-19 exactly: the narrow reading returns the reassuring 'dead'.
procedure.potency: A DEAD verdict additionally requires the mutation to have reddened at least one of that boundary-direction's own units. A mutation that reddens nothing proves nothing.
procedure.the_live_column_exclusion_set: `reddened_outside_own_and_dead` excludes a unit that lies in the own-tests of a boundary-direction recorded DEAD. The exclusion is FILE-level where every boundary-direction on that file is dead, and UNIT-level where the file is shared with a live one — otherwise excluding tool_test.exs for the dead decode side would also silence the live encode side. Both sets are listed below rather than described. THE UNIT-LEVEL FORM IS NEW AT ROUND 4 AND IT IS WHAT CATCHES THE DEAD NEIGHBOUR: a module lib/ never uses acquires no ET-CC row, so it never became a boundary, so its own-tests were never excluded, so its redness read as live-path evidence for whatever it happened to call. That is how ClientCapabilities (decode) read live at round 3 on two units in initialize_test.exs. Every one of the 21 test files contributing to a live count was checked for this and initialize_test.exs is the only one that was missing — a checked result, not a spot fix. See S7-21.

the_direction_split.antecedent: A boundary SPLITS when its lib/ module produces the asserted artefact in both directions — a decode-side producer (`from_map/1`, `decode_*`, `parse_*`) AND an encode-side producer (`defimpl`/`@derive Jason.Encoder`, `to_map/1`, `encode_*`). Applied MECHANICALLY to every boundary in the partition, not to the family the ruling was stated in front of — that would be F6 repeated inside the round that fixes F6.
the_direction_split.reach_stated_as_a_result_not_an_intentio: THE REACH IS 18 / 12 / 2, and those three categories account for all 32 module names in the partition. 18 satisfy the antecedent and are split — 36 direction rows. 12 do not and are carried single-direction, with no direction in the row id: MCP.Client, Messages.Notification and Messages.Request (hand-written encoder, no from_map), MCP.Protocol.Meta and MCP.Protocol.decode_message/1 (decode only), MCP.Protocol.Extensions (predicates and a normaliser, no wire codec), and the six PATHS rather than codecs — Server.Dispatch, Server.Connection, Server.NotificationCollector, Server.Subscription, Transport.Stdio, Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug. 2 produce the asserted artefact in ONE direction only and are recorded with that direction named: Types.Content (decode), whose from_map/1 dispatches by "type" at content.ex:32-36 and which has no encoder of its own, and Messages.Response (encode), which has @derive Jason.Encoder and a defimpl at response.ex:10 and :30 and no from_map. Neither satisfies the antecedent, so neither is split; both are named with a direction anyway because that is the only direction their bytes come from. 2*18 + 12 + 2 = 50, this file's own row count, and 36 + 2 = 38 direction-carrying rows — 19 (encode) and 19 (decode). Every one of the 19 boundary-directions this file records dead is among those 38 (6 encode, 13 decode); no undirected row is dead. F14, CORRECTED IN ROUND 6: rounds 4 and 5 said '17 modules satisfy it and are split (38 directions); 12 do not'. It accounted for 29 of the 32 names (Content and Response were in neither list); it was internally inconsistent before anyone touched the tree (17 split modules is 34 directions, and the same sentence said 38 — the 38 is right); and it was never right rather than stale, since this file has carried 18 both-direction modules since e27ca65. Guard 21 derives its split set from THIS FILE via split_modules/1 (etcc_register.ex:396-405), so the executable code and the prose about the same antecedent disagreed, in the field named 'reach stated as a result'. Found by CODE_REVIEWER at round 5, ruled by the PM at 26080. No verdict, label or count moves — nothing keys on this sentence. THE WIDER REACH CHANGED TWO VERDICTS AND ONLY TWO: ClientCapabilities (decode) and Error (encode) come back DEAD where the unsplit boundary read live. Every other direction beyond the Content family is live on BOTH sides, so for those the single round-3 verdict was sound. That is reported as a measured result — the reach question is settled by running it, not by arguing it.
the_direction_split.rule: A boundary is the PRODUCER of the asserted bytes. A `defimpl Jason.Encoder` and a `from_map/1` are different code running in opposite directions, so one direction's liveness may not carry the other (PM ruling, comment 26058).
